sentences.text: Paludohadros is a hadrosauroid ornithopod known from a single species, P. proudlovii, represented by parts of the skull, skeleton and isolated bones.
The name combines a Latin term for swamp and a Greek word meaning stout, alluding to its marshy environment and robust build.
The holotype specimen includes fragments of the skull, ribs, right shoulder girdle, forelimb pieces, right ischium, hindlimb elements and three tail vertebrae.
Its femur measures 63 cm, a length that falls between that of Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis and Comptonatus chasei.

Distinctive features comprise several ridges on the lower-jaw teeth, a dorsally projecting lateral process on the surangular, a ridge on the distal humeral condyle, a booted ischium that curves posteroventrally, and bosses on the proximal tibia.
At roughly 5 metres in length, the holotype ranks among the larger early-Cretaceous iguanodontians from the UK.
It is the inaugural dinosaur species formally described from the Barremian-aged Weald Clay of the Weald Basin.
The specific epithet honours William Proudlove, the manager of Smokejack Pit who passed away in 2000.
Unfused vertebrae and a rough (rugose) texture on limb bones suggest the individual had not yet reached full maturity.
The Weald Clay Formation records marshy, shallow floodplain settings with conifer forests and plentiful ferns, indicating a wet, vegetated habitat for Paludohadros.
Phylogenetic studies place Paludohadros as the sister taxon to Istiorachis within an early-diverging hadrosauroid clade that also contains Xuwulong and Kukufeldia.
It lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous in the United Kingdom’s Weald Clay Formation.
Other dinosaurs from the same formation include the spinosaurid Baryonyx, the indeterminate maniraptoran Wyleyia, the ankylosaur Horshamosaurus, and the dryosaurid Valdosaurus.
